docs.title: Welcome to the Data Dictionary Hub
docs.text:
Welcome to the central documentation platform for our project's database.

This platform is designed to make our data structure transparent, accessible, and easy to understand for everyone involved in the project—whether you are a developer, a data analyst, or a domain expert.

docs.title: Our Objectives
docs.text:
The main goals of this data dictionary are:

  • Single Source of Truth: Provide a reliable and standardized reference for all database entities, their attributes, and relationships.
  • Accessibility: Offer a simple, fast, and easily shareable web interface. No complex software installations or database credentials are required to understand our data.
  • Clarity & Context: Go beyond just "data types". Here you will find business definitions, constraints, example values, and specific rules (e.g., geographical data handling) for every single column.
  • Collaborative Maintenance: Empower non-technical team members to keep the documentation alive and updated through a simplified workflow.

docs.title: How to Navigate
docs.text:
Finding the information you need is quick and straightforward:

  1. Search Bar: Use the powerful search bar at the top of the page. It instantly looks through table names, column definitions, and comments.
  2. Interactive Schema: Start with the Schema Overview (ER) to get a bird's-eye view of how different tables relate to each other.
  3. Table Details: Browse the sidebar navigation menu to dive deep into specific domains and tables. Each page provides an exhaustive breakdown of the selected table.

docs.title: How to Contribute
docs.text:
Documentation is only useful if it stays up to date. We built this platform so that anyone can contribute, no coding required.

Updating the Dictionary via Excel

You don't need to know Markdown or Git to help out! We manage updates via a simple Excel template.

If you need to define a new table or update an existing description, you just need to fill out a spreadsheet containing columns like Data type, Definition, Example value, etc.

The technical team will automatically convert your Excel sheet into these web pages. Please read the Contribution Guidelines for more details.

If you find any discrepancies or have questions about specific data entities, please reach out to the database administration team.

docs.title: Graphic User Interface terminology
docs.text: The web-app application of AHEAD adopts aliases for the entities involved in the user form compilations. To improve understanding of the underlying connections to the database, this section includes a table mapping GUI interface terms to entity names in the PostgreSQL database, to support replicability and transparency of the system.

docs.title: Contribution Guidelines
docs.text:
Thank you for helping us keep the Data Dictionary accurate and up-to-date!

Good documentation is a team effort. You do not need to be a developer, know how to write code, or understand Git to contribute to this project. All content updates are managed through a simple spreadsheet.

docs.title: The Workflow
docs.text:
Updating the dictionary takes just three simple steps:

  1. Download the template: Grab the latest version of the Data Dictionary Excel template from our shared team folder.
  2. Fill in the data: Add or update the rows corresponding to the database tables and columns you are documenting.
  3. Submit for publishing: Send the updated Excel file to the technical team. We will run an automated process to convert your spreadsheet into the web pages you see here.

docs.title: How to fill out the Excel template
docs.text:
Each sheet in the Excel file represents a single database table. For every column in that table, please provide the following details:

  • Column: The exact technical name of the field in the database (e.g., user_id, geom, created_at).
  • Data type: The format of the data (e.g., VARCHAR(255), UUID, POINT, INTEGER).
  • Definition (IT) & Definition (EN): A clear, business-friendly description of what the column represents. Please fill out both the Italian and English columns to support our bilingual platform.
  • Example value: A realistic example of the data to help others understand the format (e.g., john.doe@email.com or POINT(12.49 41.89)).
  • Constraint?: Note any database rules, such as PK (Primary Key), FK (Foreign Key), or NOT NULL.
  • Geometry?: Specify if the field contains spatial data (e.g., Yes - EPSG:4326 or No).
  • Comments (IT) & Comments (EN): Any extra context, business logic, or warnings regarding how this data should be used or interpreted.

Keep Formatting Simple

Please avoid using complex Excel formatting like merged cells, custom cell colors, or multiple lines inside a single cell. Plain text ensures the smoothest conversion to the web platform!

docs.title: Submitting Your Changes
docs.text:
Once your Excel file is ready and reviewed:

  • Upload the new version to the designated shared drive.
  • Notify the database administration team via email or our internal chat.
  • The team will process the file, and your changes will be live on the Data Dictionary within a few minutes!

docs.title: Schema overview
docs.text:
The public schema is organised around three groups of tables:

  1. Enterprises: the owned, located units that can be damaged (buildings, farms, businesses, network systems).
  2. Components: the physical or economic elements that belong to an enterprise (crops, machinery, staff, road segments, and so on).
  3. Assessment: events, surveys and the damage records they produce.

Enterprises and components both use table-per-subtype inheritance: a sub-type table shares the primary key of its parent, so a row is joined to its parent with child.id = parent.id.

The schema is shown in three diagrams to keep each one readable.

• ||--o{ : One-to-Many. Example: An enterprise contains many components.
  • ||--|| : One-to-One. Example: The Building record is a direct extension of an Enterprise record.
  • }o--|| : Many-to-One. Example: Many enterprises can belong to a single owner.

docs.title: Table: added_block
docs.text:
Different name in the web-app (GUI)

In the PostgreSQL backend, this table is named added_block, as shown in the page title. In the web-app interface it appears as Added block. All aliases are listed in the correspondence table.

Description (EN): This table represents added blocks of buildings. In the database's inheritance architecture, it acts as a direct sub-type of the component table. It does not store redundant descriptive columns; instead, it uses a shared primary key to inherit all high-level attributes (such as name, location, management type, and geometry) from its parent component record.

docs.title: Column Structure
docs.text: Column Data type Definition Example value Constraint? Geometry? Comments id BIGINT Unique identifier for the added block 42 PK, FK No Primary key that also acts as a Foreign Key referencing component.id position VARCHAR [...] EXTERNAL - No [...] vertical_mat VARCHAR [...] [...] - No [...] horizontal_mat VARCHAR [...] [...] - No [...] n_floor BIGINT Number of floors of the added block 2 - No [...] total_height BIGINT Total height of the added block in [measurement unit] 200 - No [...] floor_surface BIGINT Total floor surface of the added block in [measurement unit] 200 - No [...] floor_height BIGINT Total floor height of the added block in [measurement unit] 200 - No [...] function VARCHAR [...] [...] - No [...] previous_survey VARCHAR [...] [...] - No [...]

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Inherits from (Sub-type of): component. The added_block table is a specialized extension of the component table.
  • Belongs to: enterprise (A component sub-type is linked to one enterprise)
  • Has many: damage (A component sub-type can be affected by multiple damage over time)

Where is the rest of the data?

To find the name, geographical location (geometry, town, country), or ownership details of a added_block, you must join this table with the component record that shares the exact same id.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve a list of all added blocks, including their names, towns, and spatial coordinates, by joining the table with its parent component entity:

SELECT 
    ab.id, 
    c.name, 
    c.town, 
    ST_AsText(c.geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    added_block ab
JOIN 
    component c ON ab.id = c.id
WHERE 
    c.component_kind  = 'ADDED_BLOCK';

docs.title: Table: building
docs.text:
Different name in the web-app (GUI)

In the PostgreSQL backend, this table is named building, as shown in the page title. In the web-app interface it appears as Built environment. All aliases are listed in the correspondence table.

Description (EN): This table represents buildings. In the database's inheritance architecture, it acts as a direct sub-type of the enterprise table. It does not store redundant descriptive columns; instead, it uses a shared primary key to inherit all high-level attributes (such as name, location, management type, and geometry) from its parent enterprise record.

The structural, economic and physical characteristics of a building (construction year, materials, number of floors, cost, and so on) are stored in the building_component table.

docs.title: Column Structure
docs.text: Column Data type Definition Example value Constraint? Geometry? Comments id BIGINT Building unique identifier 3 PK, FK No Primary key that also acts as a Foreign Key referencing enterprise.id

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Inherits from (Sub-type of): enterprise. The building table is a specialized extension of the enterprise table.
  • Contains: While not linked directly via a building_id, a building owns its physical parts through the enterprise_id column in the component table. These components often include specialized sub-types such as:
    • building_component
    • added_block
    • building_functionality

Where is the rest of the data?

To find the name, geographical location (geometry, town, country), or VAT of a building, you must join this table with the enterprise record that shares the exact same id. The structural and economic characteristics are in building_component, which is linked to the building through component.enterprise_id.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve the characteristics of each building by joining its enterprise record with its building components:

SELECT
    e.name,
    e.town,
    bc.n_floors,
    bc.construction_cost,
    bc.economic_value
FROM
    building b
JOIN
    enterprise e ON b.id = e.id
JOIN
    component c ON c.enterprise_id = e.id
JOIN
    building_component bc ON bc.id = c.id
WHERE
    e.type = 'BUILDING';

docs.title: Table: damage_agriculture_product
docs.text: Description (EN): This table represents damages reported to agriculture products. In the database's inheritance architecture, it acts as a direct sub-type of the farm_damage table, which is itself a sub-type of damage.   • Is reported by: survey (One or more damages is reported in a survey)
  • Reported in: attachment (A damage is reported in one or more attachments)
  • Results in: economic_loss

Where is the rest of the data?

To find the description, dates, geographical location (geometry, town, country), or other details of a damage to agriculture products, you must join this table with the damage record that shares the exact same id.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve a list of all damages to agriculture products, including their descriptions, towns, and spatial coordinates, by joining the table with its parent damage entity:

SELECT
    dap.*,
    d.*
FROM 
    damage_agriculture_product dap JOIN damage d ON dap.id = d.id;

docs.title: Table: enterprise
docs.text: Description (EN): This is the core parent entity (superclass) of the database. It stores the universal, high-level attributes, such as identification, geographical location and administrative details, for all major physical or business assets. Specific types of enterprises (like buildings, businesses, farms or network systems) store their specialized data in separate sub-tables that share the same ID. Ownership is not stored here: it is recorded in the bridge table enterprise_owner.

docs.title: Column Structure
docs.text: Column Data type Definition Example value Constraint? Geometry? Comments id BIGINT Unique identifier for the enterprise 3 PK No Acts as the universal ID across all sub-type tables type VARCHAR(255) Discriminator column defining the specific type of enterprise BUILDING NOT NULL No Values currently present in the data: 'BUILDING', 'FARM', 'TRANSPORT', 'TELECOMMUNICATION' name VARCHAR(255) Official name or denomination of the enterprise Main Headquarters No management_type VARCHAR(255) Type of management or business administration PUBLIC No e.g., 'PUBLIC', 'PRIVATE', 'MIXED' vat VARCHAR(255) VAT number of the enterprise IT00000000000 No description VARCHAR(255) Free-text description of the enterprise Regional hospital No country VARCHAR(255) Country where the enterprise is located Italy No state VARCHAR(255) State or region where the enterprise is located Lazio No county VARCHAR(255) County or province where the enterprise is located Rome No town VARCHAR(255) Municipality where the enterprise is located Rome No hamlet VARCHAR(255) Hamlet or locality where the enterprise is located Trastevere No road VARCHAR(255) Street where the enterprise is located Via Appia No house_number VARCHAR(255) House number of the enterprise 10 No postcode VARCHAR(255) Postal code of the enterprise 00100 No geometry GEOMETRY Spatial representation of the enterprise POINT(12.49 41.89) Yes EPSG:4326. Can be a Point or a Polygon depending on the scale coordinates_inferred BOOLEAN Whether the coordinates of the enterprise were inferred rather than directly measured [...] No

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Because enterprise is the central hub of the schema, it has extensive relationships:

  • Has Sub-types (Inheritance): The following tables inherit from enterprise and share its id:
    • building
    • business
    • farm
    • network_system
  • Is owned by: owner. An enterprise can have several owners, and an owner can hold several enterprises. This many-to-many relationship is mediated by the enterprise_owner bridge table.
  • Has many: component (An enterprise is composed of multiple sub-components like machinery, crops, or electrical networks)
  • Has many: survey (An enterprise can undergo multiple damage or assessment surveys over time)

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve a list of all enterprises located in a specific town, displaying their name, their specific classification (type), and their coordinates:

SELECT 
    id, 
    name, 
    type, 
    ST_AsText(geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    enterprise 
WHERE 
    town = 'Rome'
ORDER BY 
    type ASC;

Retrieve the owners of each enterprise through the bridge table:

SELECT 
    e.id, 
    e.name, 
    o.full_name 
FROM 
    enterprise e
JOIN 
    enterprise_owner eo ON eo.enterprise_id = e.id
JOIN 
    owner o ON o.id = eo.owner_id;

docs.text:
• Inherits from (Sub-type of): component. The product table is a specialized extension of the component table.
  • Belongs to: enterprise (A component sub-type is linked to one enterprise)
  • Has many: damage (A component sub-type can be affected by multiple damage over time)

Where is the rest of the data?

To find the name, geographical location (geometry, town, country), or ownership details of a product, you must join this table with the component record that shares the exact same id.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve a list of all products, including their names, towns, and spatial coordinates, by joining the table with its parent component entity:

SELECT 
    p.id, 
    c.name, 
    c.town, 
    ST_AsText(c.geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    product p 
JOIN 
    component c ON p.id = c.id

Benvenuto nella piattaforma centrale di documentazione per il database del nostro progetto.

Questa piattaforma è pensata per rendere la struttura dei nostri dati trasparente, accessibile e facile da capire per tutte le persone coinvolte nel progetto, che siano sviluppatori, analisti di dati o esperti del settore.

docs.title: I nostri obiettivi
docs.text:
Gli scopi principali di questo dizionario dati sono:

  • Unica fonte di verità: Fornire un riferimento affidabile e standardizzato per tutte le entità del database, i loro attributi e le loro relazioni.
  • Accessibilità: Offrire un'interfaccia web semplice, veloce e facilmente condivisibile. Non servono installazioni software complesse né credenziali del database per comprendere i nostri dati.
  • Chiarezza e contesto: Andare oltre i semplici “tipi di dato”. Qui trovi definizioni di business, vincoli, valori di esempio e regole specifiche (ad es. la gestione dei dati geografici) per ogni singola colonna.
  • Manutenzione collaborativa: Permettere ai membri del team non tecnici di mantenere viva e aggiornata la documentazione attraverso un flusso di lavoro semplificato.

docs.title: Come navigare
docs.text:
Trovare le informazioni di cui hai bisogno è rapido e intuitivo:

  1. Barra di ricerca: Usa la potente barra di ricerca in cima alla pagina. Cerca all'istante tra i nomi delle tabelle, le definizioni delle colonne e i commenti.
  2. Schema interattivo: Parti dalla panoramica dello schema (ER) per avere una visione d'insieme di come le diverse tabelle si relazionano tra loro.
  3. Dettagli delle tabelle: Esplora il menu di navigazione laterale per approfondire domini e tabelle specifiche. Ogni pagina offre una descrizione esaustiva della tabella selezionata.

docs.title: Come contribuire
docs.text:
La documentazione è utile solo se resta aggiornata. Abbiamo costruito questa piattaforma in modo che chiunque possa contribuire, senza scrivere codice.

Aggiornare il dizionario tramite Excel

Non serve conoscere Markdown o Git per dare una mano! Gestiamo gli aggiornamenti tramite un semplice template Excel.

Se devi definire una nuova tabella o aggiornare una descrizione esistente, ti basta compilare un foglio di calcolo con colonne come Data type, Definition, Example value, ecc.

Il team tecnico convertirà automaticamente il tuo foglio Excel in queste pagine web. Leggi le linee guida per contribuire per maggiori dettagli.

Se riscontri discrepanze o hai domande su specifiche entità di dati, contatta il team di amministrazione del database.

Grazie per aiutarci a mantenere il dizionario dati accurato e aggiornato!

Una buona documentazione è un lavoro di squadra. Non è necessario essere sviluppatori, saper programmare o conoscere Git per contribuire a questo progetto. Tutti gli aggiornamenti dei contenuti sono gestiti tramite un semplice foglio di calcolo.

docs.title: Il flusso di lavoro
docs.text:
Aggiornare il dizionario richiede solo tre semplici passaggi:

  1. Scarica il template: Recupera l'ultima versione del template Excel del dizionario dati dalla nostra cartella condivisa del team.
  2. Compila i dati: Aggiungi o aggiorna le righe corrispondenti alle tabelle e alle colonne del database che stai documentando.
  3. Invia per la pubblicazione: Invia il file Excel aggiornato al team tecnico. Eseguiremo un processo automatico per convertire il tuo foglio di calcolo nelle pagine web che vedi qui.

docs.title: Come compilare il template Excel
docs.text:
Ogni foglio del file Excel rappresenta una singola tabella del database. Per ogni colonna di quella tabella, fornisci i seguenti dettagli:

  • Column: Il nome tecnico esatto del campo nel database (ad es. user_id, geom, created_at).
  • Data type: Il formato del dato (ad es. VARCHAR(255), UUID, POINT, INTEGER).
  • Definition (IT) & Definition (EN): Una descrizione chiara e comprensibile anche ai non addetti ai lavori di ciò che la colonna rappresenta. Compila sia la colonna italiana sia quella inglese, per supportare la nostra piattaforma bilingue.
  • Example value: Un esempio realistico del dato, per aiutare gli altri a capirne il formato (ad es. john.doe@email.com o POINT(12.49 41.89)).
  • Constraint?: Indica eventuali regole del database, come PK (chiave primaria), FK (chiave esterna) o NOT NULL.
  • Geometry?: Specifica se il campo contiene dati spaziali (ad es. Yes - EPSG:4326 o No).
  • Comments (IT) & Comments (EN): Qualsiasi contesto aggiuntivo, logica di business o avvertenza su come usare o interpretare questo dato.

Mantieni la formattazione semplice

Evita formattazioni Excel complesse, come celle unite, colori personalizzati delle celle o più righe all'interno di una stessa cella. Il testo semplice garantisce la conversione più fluida verso la piattaforma web!

docs.title: Inviare le modifiche
docs.text:
Quando il tuo file Excel è pronto e rivisto:

  • Carica la nuova versione nell'unità condivisa designata.
  • Avvisa il team di amministrazione del database via email o tramite la nostra chat interna.
  • Il team elaborerà il file e le tue modifiche saranno pubblicate nel dizionario dati nel giro di pochi minuti!

docs.title: Panoramica dello schema
docs.text:
Traduzione assistita dall'IA

Questa pagina è stata tradotta con l'assistenza dell'intelligenza artificiale e può contenere imprecisioni. La versione inglese è il riferimento. I nomi delle tabelle e degli attributi sono identici in tutte le lingue perché corrispondono a quelli dell'implementazione PostgreSQL.

Lo schema public è organizzato in tre gruppi di tabelle:

  1. Imprese: le unità di proprietà e localizzate che possono subire danni (edifici, aziende agricole, attività commerciali, sistemi di rete).
  2. Componenti: gli elementi fisici o economici che appartengono a un'impresa (colture, macchinari, personale, tratti stradali e così via).
  3. Valutazione: eventi, rilevamenti e i record di danno che ne derivano.

Imprese e componenti usano entrambi l'ereditarietà con una tabella per sottotipo: la tabella di un sottotipo condivide la chiave primaria della tabella genitore, quindi una riga si collega alla sua tabella genitore con child.id = parent.id.

docs.title: Query di esempio
docs.text:
Recupera le caratteristiche di ciascun edificio unendo il relativo record di impresa con i suoi componenti edilizi:

SELECT
    e.name,
    e.town,
    bc.n_floors,
    bc.construction_cost,
    bc.economic_value
FROM
    building b
JOIN
    enterprise e ON b.id = e.id
JOIN
    component c ON c.enterprise_id = e.id
JOIN
    building_component bc ON bc.id = c.id
WHERE
    e.type = 'BUILDING';

    component c ON en.id = c.id

Descrizione (IT): Questa è l'entità genitore principale (superclasse) del database. Memorizza gli attributi universali di alto livello, come l'identificazione, la posizione geografica e i dettagli amministrativi, per tutti i principali asset fisici o aziendali. I tipi specifici di imprese (come edifici, attività commerciali, aziende agricole o sistemi di rete) memorizzano i propri dati specializzati in sotto-tabelle separate che condividono lo stesso ID. La proprietà non è memorizzata qui: è registrata nella tabella di collegamento enterprise_owner.

docs.title: Relazioni
docs.text:
Poiché enterprise è il nodo centrale dello schema, ha numerose relazioni:

  • Ha sottotipi (ereditarietà): Le tabelle seguenti ereditano da enterprise e condividono il suo id:
    • building
    • business
    • farm
    • network_system
  • È posseduta da: owner. Un'impresa può avere più proprietari e un proprietario può detenere più imprese. Questa relazione molti-a-molti è mediata dalla tabella di collegamento enterprise_owner.
  • Ha molti: component (Un'impresa è composta da più sotto-componenti, come macchinari, colture o reti elettriche)
  • Ha molti: survey (Un'impresa può essere oggetto di più danni o rilevamenti di valutazione nel tempo)

docs.title: Query di esempio
docs.text:
Recupera un elenco di tutte le imprese situate in un comune specifico, mostrando il loro nome, la loro classificazione specifica (tipo) e le loro coordinate:

SELECT 
    id, 
    name, 
    type, 
    ST_AsText(geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    enterprise 
WHERE 
    town = 'Rome'
ORDER BY 
    type ASC;

Recupera i proprietari di ciascuna impresa attraverso la tabella di collegamento:

SELECT 
    e.id, 
    e.name, 
    o.full_name 
FROM 
    enterprise e
JOIN 
    enterprise_owner eo ON eo.enterprise_id = e.id
JOIN 
    owner o ON o.id = eo.owner_id;

docs.title: Relazioni
docs.text:
• Eredita da (sottotipo di): enterprise. La tabella farm è un'estensione specializzata della tabella enterprise.
  • Contiene: Pur non essendo collegata direttamente tramite farm_id, un'azienda agricola possiede asset agricoli attraverso la colonna enterprise_id della tabella component. Questi componenti includono spesso sottotipi agricoli specializzati, come:
    • agriculture_product e i suoi sottotipi crop e stored
    • livestock
    • fixed_asset e i suoi sottotipi (ad es. machinery, come i trattori)

Dove si trova il resto dei dati?

Per trovare il nome, la posizione geografica (geometry, town, country) o altri dettagli di un'azienda agricola, devi unire questa tabella con il record enterprise che condivide lo stesso id.

docs.title: Query di esempio
docs.text:
Recupera un elenco di tutte le aziende agricole, includendo nomi, comuni e coordinate spaziali, unendo la tabella con la sua entità genitore enterprise:

SELECT 
    f.id, 
    e.name, 
    e.town, 
    ST_AsText(e.geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    farm f
JOIN 
    enterprise e ON f.id = e.id
WHERE 
    e.type = 'FARM';

docs.title: Bienvenue sur le Hub du dictionnaire de données
docs.text:
Traduction assistée par IA

Cette page a été traduite avec l'assistance de l'intelligence artificielle et peut contenir des erreurs. La version anglaise fait foi. Les noms des tables et des attributs sont identiques dans toutes les langues car ils correspondent à ceux de l'implémentation PostgreSQL.

Bienvenue sur la plateforme centrale de documentation de la base de données de notre projet.

Cette plateforme est conçue pour rendre la structure de nos données transparente, accessible et facile à comprendre pour toutes les personnes impliquées dans le projet, qu'il s'agisse de développeurs, d'analystes de données ou d'experts du domaine.

docs.title: Nos objectifs
docs.text:
Les principaux objectifs de ce dictionnaire de données sont les suivants :

  • Source unique de vérité : Fournir une référence fiable et normalisée pour toutes les entités de la base de données, leurs attributs et leurs relations.
  • Accessibilité : Proposer une interface web simple, rapide et facile à partager. Aucune installation logicielle complexe ni aucun identifiant de base de données n'est nécessaire pour comprendre nos données.
  • Clarté et contexte : Aller au-delà des simples « types de données ». Vous y trouverez des définitions métier, des contraintes, des exemples de valeurs et des règles spécifiques (p. ex. le traitement des données géographiques) pour chaque colonne.
  • Maintenance collaborative : Permettre aux membres de l'équipe non techniques de garder la documentation vivante et à jour grâce à un flux de travail simplifié.

docs.title: Comment naviguer
docs.text:
Trouver l'information dont vous avez besoin est rapide et simple :

  1. Barre de recherche : Utilisez la puissante barre de recherche en haut de la page. Elle parcourt instantanément les noms des tables, les définitions des colonnes et les commentaires.
  2. Schéma interactif : Commencez par l'aperçu du schéma (ER) pour avoir une vue d'ensemble des relations entre les différentes tables.
  3. Détail des tables : Parcourez le menu de navigation latéral pour explorer en détail des domaines et des tables spécifiques. Chaque page propose une description exhaustive de la table sélectionnée.

docs.title: Comment contribuer
docs.text:
Une documentation n'est utile que si elle reste à jour. Nous avons conçu cette plateforme pour que tout le monde puisse contribuer, sans écrire de code.

Mettre à jour le dictionnaire via Excel

Pas besoin de connaître Markdown ou Git pour donner un coup de main ! Nous gérons les mises à jour grâce à un simple modèle Excel.

Si vous devez définir une nouvelle table ou mettre à jour une description existante, il vous suffit de remplir un tableur contenant des colonnes comme Data type, Definition, Example value, etc.

L'équipe technique convertira automatiquement votre feuille Excel en ces pages web. Veuillez lire le guide de contribution pour plus de détails.

Si vous constatez des divergences ou si vous avez des questions sur des entités de données spécifiques, veuillez contacter l'équipe d'administration de la base de données.

L'application web de AHEAD utilise des alias pour les entités concernées par la saisie des formulaires par les utilisateurs. Pour faciliter la compréhension des liens sous-jacents avec la base de données, cette section comprend un tableau qui associe les termes de l'interface graphique aux noms des entités de la base de données PostgreSQL, afin de favoriser la reproductibilité et la transparence du système.

docs.title: Guide de contribution
docs.text:
Traduction assistée par IA

Cette page a été traduite avec l'assistance de l'intelligence artificielle et peut contenir des erreurs. La version anglaise fait foi. Les noms des tables et des attributs sont identiques dans toutes les langues car ils correspondent à ceux de l'implémentation PostgreSQL.

Merci de nous aider à maintenir le dictionnaire de données exact et à jour !

Une bonne documentation est un travail d'équipe. Vous n'avez pas besoin d'être développeur, de savoir programmer ni de connaître Git pour contribuer à ce projet. Toutes les mises à jour de contenu sont gérées à l'aide d'un simple tableur.

docs.title: Le flux de travail
docs.text:
La mise à jour du dictionnaire ne demande que trois étapes simples :

  1. Télécharger le modèle : Récupérez la dernière version du modèle Excel du dictionnaire de données dans notre dossier d'équipe partagé.
  2. Renseigner les données : Ajoutez ou mettez à jour les lignes correspondant aux tables et aux colonnes de la base de données que vous documentez.
  3. Soumettre pour publication : Envoyez le fichier Excel mis à jour à l'équipe technique. Nous lancerons un processus automatisé pour convertir votre tableur en pages web, comme celles que vous voyez ici.

docs.title: Comment remplir le modèle Excel
docs.text:
Chaque feuille du fichier Excel représente une seule table de la base de données. Pour chaque colonne de cette table, veuillez fournir les informations suivantes :

  • Column: Le nom technique exact du champ dans la base de données (p. ex. user_id, geom, created_at).
  • Data type: Le format de la donnée (p. ex. VARCHAR(255), UUID, POINT, INTEGER).
  • Definition (IT) & Definition (EN): Une description claire, compréhensible aussi par des non-spécialistes, de ce que représente la colonne. Veuillez remplir à la fois la colonne italienne et la colonne anglaise, afin de soutenir notre plateforme bilingue.
  • Example value: Un exemple réaliste de la donnée pour aider les autres à comprendre son format (p. ex. john.doe@email.com ou POINT(12.49 41.89)).
  • Constraint?: Indiquez les éventuelles règles de la base de données, comme PK (clé primaire), FK (clé étrangère) ou NOT NULL.
  • Geometry?: Précisez si le champ contient des données spatiales (p. ex. Yes - EPSG:4326 ou No).
  • Comments (IT) & Comments (EN): Tout contexte supplémentaire, règle métier ou avertissement sur la façon d'utiliser ou d'interpréter cette donnée.

Gardez une mise en forme simple

Veuillez éviter les mises en forme Excel complexes, comme les cellules fusionnées, les couleurs de cellule personnalisées ou les retours à la ligne multiples dans une même cellule. Un texte brut garantit la conversion la plus fluide vers la plateforme web !

docs.title: Soumettre vos modifications
docs.text:
Une fois votre fichier Excel prêt et relu :

  • Téléversez la nouvelle version sur le lecteur partagé désigné.
  • Informez l'équipe d'administration de la base de données par e-mail ou via notre messagerie interne.
  • L'équipe traitera le fichier et vos modifications seront en ligne dans le dictionnaire de données en quelques minutes !

docs.title: Aperçu du schéma
docs.text:
Traduction assistée par IA

Cette page a été traduite avec l'assistance de l'intelligence artificielle et peut contenir des erreurs. La version anglaise fait foi. Les noms des tables et des attributs sont identiques dans toutes les langues car ils correspondent à ceux de l'implémentation PostgreSQL.

Le schéma public est organisé autour de trois groupes de tables :

  1. Entreprises : les unités détenues et localisées qui peuvent être endommagées (bâtiments, exploitations agricoles, entreprises commerciales, systèmes de réseau).
  2. Composants : les éléments physiques ou économiques qui appartiennent à une entreprise (cultures, machines, personnel, tronçons de route, etc.).
  3. Évaluation : les événements, les relevés et les enregistrements de dommages qu'ils produisent.

Les entreprises et les composants utilisent tous deux l'héritage à une table par sous-type : la table d'un sous-type partage la clé primaire de sa table parente, de sorte qu'une ligne est jointe à sa table parente avec child.id = parent.id.

Le schéma est présenté en trois diagrammes afin que chacun reste lisible.

• ||--o{ : Un-à-plusieurs. Exemple : une entreprise contient plusieurs composants.

Description (FR) : Cette table représente les blocs ajoutés aux bâtiments. Dans l'architecture d'héritage de la base de données, elle joue le rôle de sous-type direct de la table component. Elle ne stocke pas de colonnes descriptives redondantes : elle utilise à la place une clé primaire partagée pour hériter de tous les attributs de haut niveau (comme le nom, la localisation, le type de gestion et la géométrie) de son enregistrement parent component.

docs.text:
• Hérite de (sous-type de) : component. La table added_block est une extension spécialisée de la table component.
  • Appartient à : enterprise (Un sous-type de composant est lié à une seule entreprise)
  • A plusieurs : damage (Un sous-type de composant peut subir plusieurs dommages au fil du temps)

Où trouver le reste des données ?

Pour trouver le nom, la localisation géographique (geometry, town, country) ou les informations de propriété d'un enregistrement added_block, vous devez joindre cette table à l'enregistrement component qui partage le même id.

docs.title: Exemple de requête
docs.text:
Récupérez la liste de tous les blocs ajoutés, avec leurs noms, communes et coordonnées spatiales, en joignant la table à son entité parente component :

SELECT 
    ab.id, 
    c.name, 
    c.town, 
    ST_AsText(c.geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    added_block ab
JOIN 
    component c ON ab.id = c.id
WHERE 
    c.component_kind  = 'ADDED_BLOCK';

Description (FR) : Cette table représente les bâtiments. Dans l'architecture d'héritage de la base de données, elle joue le rôle de sous-type direct de la table enterprise. Elle ne stocke pas de colonnes descriptives redondantes : elle utilise à la place une clé primaire partagée pour hériter de tous les attributs de haut niveau (comme le nom, la localisation, le type de gestion et la géométrie) de son enregistrement parent enterprise.

Les caractéristiques structurelles, économiques et physiques d'un bâtiment (année de construction, matériaux, nombre d'étages, coût, etc.) sont stockées dans la table building_component.

docs.title: Structure des colonnes
docs.text: Colonne Type de données Définition Exemple de valeur Contrainte ? Géométrie ? Commentaires id BIGINT Identifiant unique du bâtiment 3 PK, FK Non Clé primaire qui joue aussi le rôle de clé étrangère référençant enterprise.id

docs.title: Relations
docs.text:
• Hérite de (sous-type de) : enterprise. La table building est une extension spécialisée de la table enterprise.
  • Contient : Bien qu'il ne soit pas lié directement via building_id, un bâtiment possède ses parties physiques par la colonne enterprise_id de la table component. Ces composants incluent souvent des sous-types spécialisés, tels que :
    • building_component
    • added_block
    • building_functionality

Où trouver le reste des données ?

Pour trouver le nom, la localisation géographique (geometry, town, country) ou le numéro de TVA d'un bâtiment, vous devez joindre cette table à l'enregistrement enterprise qui partage le même id. Les caractéristiques structurelles et économiques se trouvent dans building_component, qui est liée au bâtiment par component.enterprise_id.

docs.title: Exemple de requête
docs.text:
Récupérez les caractéristiques de chaque bâtiment en joignant son enregistrement d'entreprise à ses composants de bâtiment :

SELECT
    e.name,
    e.town,
    bc.n_floors,
    bc.construction_cost,
    bc.economic_value
FROM
    building b
JOIN
    enterprise e ON b.id = e.id
JOIN
    component c ON c.enterprise_id = e.id
JOIN
    building_component bc ON bc.id = c.id
WHERE
    e.type = 'BUILDING';

Comme enterprise est le pivot central du schéma, elle a de nombreuses relations :

docs.title: Exemple de requête
docs.text:

SELECT

    name, 
    type, 
    ST_AsText(geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    enterprise 
WHERE 
    town = 'Rome'
ORDER BY 
    type ASC;

SELECT 
    e.id,

    o.full_name 
FROM 
    enterprise e
JOIN 
    enterprise_owner eo ON eo.enterprise_id = e.id

    owner o ON o.id = eo.owner_id;

Bem-vindo à plataforma central de documentação da base de dados do nosso projeto.

Esta plataforma foi concebida para tornar a estrutura dos nossos dados transparente, acessível e fácil de compreender para todas as pessoas envolvidas no projeto, sejam programadores, analistas de dados ou especialistas na matéria.

docs.title: Os nossos objetivos
docs.text:
Os principais objetivos deste dicionário de dados são:

  • Fonte única de verdade: Fornecer uma referência fiável e normalizada para todas as entidades da base de dados, os seus atributos e as suas relações.
  • Acessibilidade: Oferecer uma interface web simples, rápida e fácil de partilhar. Não são necessárias instalações de software complexas nem credenciais da base de dados para compreender os nossos dados.
  • Clareza e contexto: Ir além dos simples “tipos de dados”. Aqui encontra definições de negócio, restrições, exemplos de valores e regras específicas (p. ex. o tratamento de dados geográficos) para cada coluna.
  • Manutenção colaborativa: Permitir que os membros da equipa não técnicos mantenham a documentação viva e atualizada através de um fluxo de trabalho simplificado.

docs.title: Como navegar
docs.text:
Encontrar a informação de que precisa é rápido e simples:

  1. Barra de pesquisa: Utilize a poderosa barra de pesquisa no topo da página. Pesquisa instantaneamente nos nomes das tabelas, nas definições das colunas e nos comentários.
  2. Esquema interativo: Comece pela visão geral do esquema (ER) para ter uma perspetiva global de como as diferentes tabelas se relacionam entre si.
  3. Detalhes das tabelas: Explore o menu de navegação lateral para aprofundar domínios e tabelas específicos. Cada página apresenta uma descrição exaustiva da tabela selecionada.

docs.title: Como contribuir
docs.text:
A documentação só é útil se se mantiver atualizada. Construímos esta plataforma para que qualquer pessoa possa contribuir, sem necessidade de escrever código.

Atualizar o dicionário através do Excel

Não precisa de saber Markdown nem Git para ajudar! Gerimos as atualizações através de um simples modelo Excel.

Se precisar de definir uma nova tabela ou de atualizar uma descrição existente, basta preencher uma folha de cálculo com colunas como Data type, Definition, Example value, etc.

A equipa técnica converterá automaticamente a sua folha Excel nestas páginas web. Leia as diretrizes de contribuição para mais detalhes.

Se encontrar discrepâncias ou tiver dúvidas sobre entidades de dados específicas, contacte a equipa de administração da base de dados.

docs.text:

Obrigado por nos ajudar a manter o dicionário de dados rigoroso e atualizado!

Uma boa documentação é um trabalho de equipa. Não precisa de ser programador, de saber escrever código nem de conhecer o Git para contribuir para este projeto. Todas as atualizações de conteúdo são geridas através de uma simples folha de cálculo.

docs.title: O fluxo de trabalho
docs.text:
Atualizar o dicionário requer apenas três passos simples:

  1. Descarregar o modelo: Obtenha a versão mais recente do modelo Excel do dicionário de dados na nossa pasta partilhada da equipa.
  2. Preencher os dados: Adicione ou atualize as linhas correspondentes às tabelas e às colunas da base de dados que está a documentar.
  3. Submeter para publicação: Envie o ficheiro Excel atualizado à equipa técnica. Executaremos um processo automático para converter a sua folha de cálculo nas páginas web que vê aqui.

docs.title: Como preencher o modelo Excel
docs.text:
Cada folha do ficheiro Excel representa uma única tabela da base de dados. Para cada coluna dessa tabela, indique os seguintes detalhes:

  • Column: O nome técnico exato do campo na base de dados (p. ex. user_id, geom, created_at).
  • Data type: O formato dos dados (p. ex. VARCHAR(255), UUID, POINT, INTEGER).
  • Definition (IT) & Definition (EN): Uma descrição clara, compreensível também por quem não é da área, do que a coluna representa. Preencha tanto a coluna italiana como a inglesa, para apoiar a nossa plataforma bilingue.
  • Example value: Um exemplo realista dos dados, para ajudar os outros a compreender o formato (p. ex. john.doe@email.com ou POINT(12.49 41.89)).
  • Constraint?: Indique eventuais regras da base de dados, como PK (chave primária), FK (chave estrangeira) ou NOT NULL.
  • Geometry?: Especifique se o campo contém dados espaciais (p. ex. Yes - EPSG:4326 ou No).
  • Comments (IT) & Comments (EN): Qualquer contexto adicional, lógica de negócio ou aviso sobre a forma de utilizar ou interpretar estes dados.

Mantenha a formatação simples

Evite formatações Excel complexas, como células intercaladas, cores de células personalizadas ou várias linhas dentro de uma mesma célula. O texto simples garante a conversão mais fluida para a plataforma web!

docs.title: Submeter as alterações
docs.text:
Quando o seu ficheiro Excel estiver pronto e revisto:

  • Carregue a nova versão na unidade partilhada designada.
  • Avise a equipa de administração da base de dados por e-mail ou através do nosso chat interno.
  • A equipa processará o ficheiro e as suas alterações ficarão disponíveis no dicionário de dados em poucos minutos!

O esquema public está organizado em três grupos de tabelas:

  1. Empresas: as unidades detidas e localizadas que podem sofrer danos (edifícios, explorações agrícolas, empresas comerciais, sistemas de rede).
  2. Componentes: os elementos físicos ou económicos que pertencem a uma empresa (culturas, maquinaria, pessoal, troços de estrada, etc.).
  3. Avaliação: eventos, levantamentos e os registos de danos que estes originam.

As empresas e os componentes usam ambos a herança com uma tabela por subtipo: a tabela de um subtipo partilha a chave primária da tabela-mãe, pelo que uma linha é associada à sua tabela-mãe com child.id = parent.id.

docs.title: Consulta de exemplo
docs.text:

SELECT
    e.name,
    e.town,
    bc.n_floors,
    bc.construction_cost,
    bc.economic_value
FROM
    building b
JOIN
    enterprise e ON b.id = e.id
JOIN
    component c ON c.enterprise_id = e.id
JOIN
    building_component bc ON bc.id = c.id
WHERE
    e.type = 'BUILDING';

Descrição (PT): Esta é a entidade-mãe central (superclasse) da base de dados. Armazena os atributos universais de alto nível, como a identificação, a localização geográfica e os dados administrativos, de todos os principais ativos físicos ou empresariais. Os tipos específicos de empresas (como edifícios, empresas comerciais, explorações agrícolas ou sistemas de rede) armazenam os seus dados especializados em subtabelas separadas que partilham o mesmo ID. A propriedade não é armazenada aqui: está registada na tabela de ligação enterprise_owner.

docs.title: Relações
docs.text:
Dado que enterprise é o eixo central do esquema, tem numerosas relações:

  • Tem subtipos (herança): As tabelas seguintes herdam de enterprise e partilham o seu id:
    • building
    • business
    • farm
    • network_system
  • É detida por: owner. Uma empresa pode ter vários proprietários e um proprietário pode deter várias empresas. Esta relação muitos-para-muitos é assegurada pela tabela de ligação enterprise_owner.
  • Tem muitos: component (Uma empresa é composta por vários subcomponentes, como maquinaria, culturas ou redes elétricas)
  • Tem muitos: survey (Uma empresa pode ser objeto de vários danos ou levantamentos de avaliação ao longo do tempo)

docs.title: Consulta de exemplo
docs.text:
Obtenha uma lista de todas as empresas situadas num município específico, mostrando o seu nome, a sua classificação específica (tipo) e as suas coordenadas:

SELECT 
    id, 
    name, 
    type, 
    ST_AsText(geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    enterprise 
WHERE 
    town = 'Rome'
ORDER BY 
    type ASC;

Obtenha os proprietários de cada empresa através da tabela de ligação:

SELECT 
    e.id, 
    e.name, 
    o.full_name 
FROM 
    enterprise e
JOIN 
    enterprise_owner eo ON eo.enterprise_id = e.id
JOIN 
    owner o ON o.id = eo.owner_id;

docs.title: Tabela: farm
docs.text:
Nome diferente na interface web (GUI)

No backend PostgreSQL, esta tabela chama-se farm, como indicado no título da página. Na interface da aplicação web aparece como Economic Activities - Farm. Todos os aliases estão na tabela de correspondência.

Tradução assistida por IA

Esta página foi traduzida com a assistência de inteligência artificial e pode conter erros. A versão em inglês é a referência. Os nomes das tabelas e dos atributos são idênticos em todas as línguas porque correspondem aos da implementação PostgreSQL.

Descrição (PT): Esta tabela representa as empresas agrícolas. Na arquitetura de herança da base de dados, funciona como subtipo direto da tabela enterprise. Não armazena colunas descritivas redundantes: em vez disso, utiliza uma chave primária partilhada para herdar todos os atributos de alto nível (como nome, localização, tipo de gestão e geometria) do seu registo principal enterprise.

docs.title: Estrutura das colunas
docs.text: Coluna Tipo de dados Definição Exemplo de valor Restrição? Geometria? Comentários id BIGINT Identificador único da exploração agrícola 42 PK, FK Não Chave primária que funciona também como chave estrangeira a referenciar enterprise.id

docs.title: Relações
docs.text:
• Herda de (subtipo de): enterprise. A tabela farm é uma extensão especializada da tabela enterprise.
  • Contém: Embora não esteja ligada diretamente através de farm_id, uma exploração agrícola possui ativos agrícolas através da coluna enterprise_id da tabela component. Estes componentes incluem frequentemente subtipos agrícolas especializados, tais como:
    • agriculture_product e os seus subtipos crop e stored
    • livestock
    • fixed_asset e os seus subtipos (p. ex. machinery, como tratores)

Onde está o resto dos dados?

Para encontrar o nome, a localização geográfica (geometry, town, country) ou outros detalhes de uma exploração agrícola, tem de juntar esta tabela ao registo enterprise que partilha o mesmo id.

docs.title: Consulta de exemplo
docs.text:
Obtenha uma lista de todas as explorações agrícolas, incluindo nomes, municípios e coordenadas espaciais, juntando a tabela à respetiva entidade-mãe enterprise:

SELECT 
    f.id, 
    e.name, 
    e.town, 
    ST_AsText(e.geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    farm f
JOIN 
    enterprise e ON f.id = e.id
WHERE 
    e.type = 'FARM';

Onde está o resto dos dados?

Para encontrar o nome, a localização geográfica (geometry, town, country) ou os detalhes de propriedade de um produto, tem de juntar esta tabela ao registo component que partilha o mesmo id.

docs.title: Consulta de exemplo
docs.text:
Obtenha uma lista de todos os produtos, incluindo nomes, municípios e coordenadas espaciais, juntando a tabela à respetiva entidade-mãe component:

SELECT 
    p.id, 
    c.name, 
    c.town, 
    ST_AsText(c.geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    product p 
JOIN 
    component c ON p.id = c.id

docs.title: Unsere Ziele
docs.text:
Die wichtigsten Ziele dieses Datenwörterbuchs sind:

  • Einheitliche Wissensgrundlage: Eine verlässliche, standardisierte Referenz für alle Datenbankentitäten, ihre Attribute und ihre Beziehungen bereitzustellen.
  • Zugänglichkeit: Eine einfache, schnelle und leicht teilbare Weboberfläche anzubieten. Für das Verständnis unserer Daten sind weder aufwendige Softwareinstallationen noch Datenbank-Zugangsdaten erforderlich.
  • Klarheit und Kontext: Über die reinen „Datentypen“ hinauszugehen. Hier finden Sie fachliche Definitionen, Einschränkungen, Beispielwerte und spezifische Regeln (z. B. zum Umgang mit Geodaten) für jede einzelne Spalte.
  • Gemeinsame Pflege: Auch Teammitglieder ohne technischen Hintergrund zu befähigen, die Dokumentation über einen vereinfachten Arbeitsablauf aktuell zu halten.

docs.title: So navigieren Sie

  1. Suchleiste: Nutzen Sie die leistungsstarke Suchleiste oben auf der Seite. Sie durchsucht sofort Tabellennamen, Spaltendefinitionen und Kommentare.
  2. Interaktives Schema: Beginnen Sie mit der Schemaübersicht (ER), um einen Überblick darüber zu erhalten, wie die verschiedenen Tabellen zueinander in Beziehung stehen.
  3. Tabellendetails: Nutzen Sie das Navigationsmenü an der Seite, um sich in bestimmte Bereiche und Tabellen zu vertiefen. Jede Seite bietet eine ausführliche Beschreibung der ausgewählten Tabelle.

docs.title: So können Sie mitwirken

Dokumentation ist nur nützlich, wenn sie aktuell bleibt. Wir haben diese Plattform so aufgebaut, dass jede und jeder mitwirken kann, ganz ohne Programmierung.

Das Wörterbuch über Excel aktualisieren

Sie müssen weder Markdown noch Git kennen, um zu helfen! Aktualisierungen verwalten wir über eine einfache Excel-Vorlage.

Wenn Sie eine neue Tabelle definieren oder eine bestehende Beschreibung aktualisieren möchten, genügt es, eine Tabellenkalkulation mit Spalten wie Data type, Definition, Example value usw. auszufüllen.

Das technische Team wandelt Ihr Excel-Blatt automatisch in diese Webseiten um. Weitere Einzelheiten finden Sie in den Hinweisen zur Mitarbeit.

Wenn Sie Unstimmigkeiten bemerken oder Fragen zu bestimmten Datenentitäten haben, wenden Sie sich bitte an das Datenbank-Administrationsteam.

docs.title: Der Arbeitsablauf
docs.text:
Die Aktualisierung des Wörterbuchs besteht nur aus drei einfachen Schritten:

  1. Vorlage herunterladen: Laden Sie die neueste Version der Excel-Vorlage des Datenwörterbuchs aus unserem gemeinsamen Teamordner herunter.
  2. Daten eintragen: Ergänzen oder aktualisieren Sie die Zeilen, die den Tabellen und Spalten der Datenbank entsprechen, die Sie dokumentieren.
  3. Zur Veröffentlichung einreichen: Senden Sie die aktualisierte Excel-Datei an das technische Team. Wir starten einen automatisierten Prozess, der Ihre Tabellenkalkulation in die Webseiten umwandelt, die Sie hier sehen.

docs.title: So füllen Sie die Excel-Vorlage aus
docs.text:
Jedes Blatt der Excel-Datei steht für eine einzelne Datenbanktabelle. Bitte machen Sie zu jeder Spalte dieser Tabelle die folgenden Angaben:

  • Column: Der genaue technische Name des Feldes in der Datenbank (z. B. user_id, geom, created_at).
  • Data type: Das Format der Daten (z. B. VARCHAR(255), UUID, POINT, INTEGER).
  • Definition (IT) & Definition (EN): Eine klare, auch für Nicht-Fachleute verständliche Beschreibung dessen, was die Spalte darstellt. Bitte füllen Sie sowohl die italienische als auch die englische Spalte aus, um unsere zweisprachige Plattform zu unterstützen.
  • Example value: Ein realistisches Beispiel für die Daten, damit andere das Format verstehen (z. B. john.doe@email.com oder POINT(12.49 41.89)).
  • Constraint?: Geben Sie vorhandene Datenbankregeln an, etwa PK (Primärschlüssel), FK (Fremdschlüssel) oder NOT NULL.
  • Geometry?: Geben Sie an, ob das Feld räumliche Daten enthält (z. B. Yes - EPSG:4326 oder No).
  • Comments (IT) & Comments (EN): Zusätzlicher Kontext, Geschäftslogik oder Hinweise dazu, wie diese Daten verwendet oder interpretiert werden sollen.

Formatierung einfach halten

Bitte vermeiden Sie aufwendige Excel-Formatierungen wie verbundene Zellen, individuelle Zellfarben oder mehrere Zeilen innerhalb einer Zelle. Einfacher Text sorgt für die reibungsloseste Umwandlung in die Webplattform!

docs.title: Änderungen einreichen
docs.text:
Sobald Ihre Excel-Datei fertig und geprüft ist:

  • Laden Sie die neue Version im vorgesehenen gemeinsamen Laufwerk hoch.
  • Informieren Sie das Datenbank-Administrationsteam per E-Mail oder über unseren internen Chat.
  • Das Team verarbeitet die Datei, und Ihre Änderungen sind innerhalb weniger Minuten im Datenwörterbuch sichtbar!

docs.title: Schemaübersicht
docs.text:
KI-gestützte Übersetzung

Diese Seite wurde mit Unterstützung künstlicher Intelligenz übersetzt und kann Fehler enthalten. Maßgeblich ist die englische Version. Die Namen der Tabellen und Attribute sind in allen Sprachen identisch, da sie der PostgreSQL-Implementierung entsprechen.

Das Schema public ist um drei Gruppen von Tabellen herum aufgebaut:

  1. Unternehmen: die im Besitz befindlichen, verorteten Einheiten, die beschädigt werden können (Gebäude, landwirtschaftliche Betriebe, Gewerbebetriebe, Netzsysteme).
  2. Komponenten: die physischen oder wirtschaftlichen Elemente, die zu einem Unternehmen gehören (Kulturen, Maschinen, Personal, Straßenabschnitte usw.).
  3. Bewertung: Ereignisse, Erhebungen und die daraus entstehenden Schadensdatensätze.

Unternehmen und Komponenten nutzen beide die Vererbung mit einer Tabelle pro Untertyp: Die Tabelle eines Untertyps teilt den Primärschlüssel der übergeordneten Tabelle, sodass eine Zeile mit child.id = parent.id mit ihrer übergeordneten Tabelle verknüpft wird.

Wo befinden sich die übrigen Daten?

Um den Namen, den geografischen Standort (geometry, town, country) oder die Eigentumsangaben eines Datensatzes added_block zu ermitteln, müssen Sie diese Tabelle mit dem Datensatz component verknüpfen, der dieselbe id besitzt.

docs.title: Beispielabfrage
docs.text:
Rufen Sie eine Liste aller Anbauten ab, einschließlich Namen, Gemeinden und räumlicher Koordinaten, indem Sie die Tabelle mit ihrer übergeordneten Entität component verknüpfen:

SELECT 
    ab.id, 
    c.name, 
    c.town, 
    ST_AsText(c.geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    added_block ab
JOIN 
    component c ON ab.id = c.id
WHERE 
    c.component_kind  = 'ADDED_BLOCK';

    • added_block

Wo befinden sich die übrigen Daten?

Die baulichen und wirtschaftlichen Merkmale befinden sich in building_component, die über component.enterprise_id mit dem Gebäude verknüpft ist.

docs.title: Beispielabfrage
docs.text:
Rufen Sie die Merkmale jedes Gebäudes ab, indem Sie dessen Unternehmensdatensatz mit seinen Gebäudekomponenten verknüpfen:

SELECT
    e.name,
    e.town,
    bc.n_floors,
    bc.construction_cost,
    bc.economic_value
FROM
    building b
JOIN
    enterprise e ON b.id = e.id
JOIN
    component c ON c.enterprise_id = e.id
JOIN
    building_component bc ON bc.id = c.id
WHERE
    e.type = 'BUILDING';

Beschreibung (DE): Dies ist die zentrale übergeordnete Entität (Oberklasse) der Datenbank. Sie speichert die universellen, übergeordneten Attribute, wie Identifikation, geografische Lage und Verwaltungsangaben, für alle wichtigen physischen oder geschäftlichen Vermögenswerte. Spezifische Unternehmenstypen (wie Gebäude, Gewerbebetriebe, landwirtschaftliche Betriebe oder Netzsysteme) speichern ihre spezialisierten Daten in separaten Untertabellen, die dieselbe ID teilen. Das Eigentum wird hier nicht gespeichert: Es wird in der Verknüpfungstabelle enterprise_owner erfasst.

Kann je nach Maßstab ein Punkt oder ein Polygon sein coordinates_inferred BOOLEAN Gibt an, ob die Koordinaten des Unternehmens abgeleitet statt direkt gemessen wurden [...] Nein

docs.title: Beziehungen
docs.text:
Da enterprise der zentrale Knotenpunkt des Schemas ist, hat sie zahlreiche Beziehungen:

  • Hat Untertypen (Vererbung): Die folgenden Tabellen erben von enterprise und teilen deren id:
    • building
    • business
    • farm
    • network_system
  • Gehört: owner. Ein Unternehmen kann mehrere Eigentümer haben, und ein Eigentümer kann mehrere Unternehmen besitzen. Diese Viele-zu-viele-Beziehung wird über die Verknüpfungstabelle enterprise_owner vermittelt.
  • Hat viele: component (Ein Unternehmen besteht aus mehreren Teilkomponenten, etwa Maschinen, Kulturen oder Stromnetzen)
  • Hat viele: survey (Ein Unternehmen kann im Laufe der Zeit mehrere Schäden oder Bewertungserhebungen erfahren)

docs.title: Beispielabfrage
docs.text:
Rufen Sie eine Liste aller Unternehmen in einer bestimmten Gemeinde ab und zeigen Sie deren Namen, deren spezifische Klassifizierung (Typ) und deren Koordinaten an:

SELECT 
    id, 
    name, 
    type, 
    ST_AsText(geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    enterprise 
WHERE 
    town = 'Rome'
ORDER BY 
    type ASC;

Rufen Sie die Eigentümer jedes Unternehmens über die Verknüpfungstabelle ab:

SELECT 
    e.id, 
    e.name, 
    o.full_name 
FROM 
    enterprise e
JOIN 
    enterprise_owner eo ON eo.enterprise_id = e.id
JOIN 
    owner o ON o.id = eo.owner_id;

docs.title: Welcome to the Data Dictionary Hub
docs.text:
Welcome to the central documentation platform for our project's database.

This platform is designed to make our data structure transparent, accessible, and easy to understand for everyone involved in the project—whether you are a developer, a data analyst, or a domain expert.

docs.title: Our Objectives
docs.text:
The main goals of this data dictionary are:

  • Single Source of Truth: Provide a reliable and standardized reference for all database entities, their attributes, and relationships.
  • Accessibility: Offer a simple, fast, and easily shareable web interface. No complex software installations or database credentials are required to understand our data.
  • Clarity & Context: Go beyond just "data types". Here you will find business definitions, constraints, example values, and specific rules (e.g., geographical data handling) for every single column.
  • Collaborative Maintenance: Empower non-technical team members to keep the documentation alive and updated through a simplified workflow.

docs.title: How to Navigate
docs.text:
Finding the information you need is quick and straightforward:

  1. Search Bar: Use the powerful search bar at the top of the page. It instantly looks through table names, column definitions, and comments.
  2. Interactive Schema: Start with the Schema Overview (ER) to get a bird's-eye view of how different tables relate to each other.
  3. Table Details: Browse the sidebar navigation menu to dive deep into specific domains and tables. Each page provides an exhaustive breakdown of the selected table.

docs.title: How to Contribute
docs.text:
Documentation is only useful if it stays up to date. We built this platform so that anyone can contribute, no coding required.

Updating the Dictionary via Excel

You don't need to know Markdown or Git to help out! We manage updates via a simple Excel template.

If you need to define a new table or update an existing description, you just need to fill out a spreadsheet containing columns like Data type, Definition, Example value, etc.

The technical team will automatically convert your Excel sheet into these web pages. Please read the Contribution Guidelines for more details.

If you find any discrepancies or have questions about specific data entities, please reach out to the database administration team.

docs.title: Graphic User Interface terminology
docs.text: The web-app application of AHEAD adopts aliases for the entities involved in the user form compilations. To improve understanding of the underlying connections to the database, this section includes a table mapping GUI interface terms to entity names in the PostgreSQL database, to support replicability and transparency of the system.

docs.title: Backend to web-app correspondence
docs.text: Entity name in the database Website alias building Built environment business Economic Activities - Business farm Economic Activities - Farm electrical_system Lifelines - Electrical transport_system Lifelines - Transport tlc_system Lifelines - Telecommunication owner Owner profiles component Elements & production (all subclasses) added_block Added block building_component Principal structure fixed_asset Elements material Stocks - Stored inputs network_service Telecom service/Electrical service/Transport service transport_network_component Transport element tlc_network_component Telecom element

docs.title: Contribution Guidelines
docs.text:
Thank you for helping us keep the Data Dictionary accurate and up-to-date!

Good documentation is a team effort. You do not need to be a developer, know how to write code, or understand Git to contribute to this project. All content updates are managed through a simple spreadsheet.

docs.title: The Workflow
docs.text:
Updating the dictionary takes just three simple steps:

  1. Download the template: Grab the latest version of the Data Dictionary Excel template from our shared team folder.
  2. Fill in the data: Add or update the rows corresponding to the database tables and columns you are documenting.
  3. Submit for publishing: Send the updated Excel file to the technical team. We will run an automated process to convert your spreadsheet into the web pages you see here.

docs.title: How to fill out the Excel template
docs.text:
Each sheet in the Excel file represents a single database table. For every column in that table, please provide the following details:

  • Column: The exact technical name of the field in the database (e.g., user_id, geom, created_at).
  • Data type: The format of the data (e.g., VARCHAR(255), UUID, POINT, INTEGER).
  • Definition (IT) & Definition (EN): A clear, business-friendly description of what the column represents. Please fill out both the Italian and English columns to support our bilingual platform.
  • Example value: A realistic example of the data to help others understand the format (e.g., john.doe@email.com or POINT(12.49 41.89)).
  • Constraint?: Note any database rules, such as PK (Primary Key), FK (Foreign Key), or NOT NULL.
  • Geometry?: Specify if the field contains spatial data (e.g., Yes - EPSG:4326 or No).
  • Comments (IT) & Comments (EN): Any extra context, business logic, or warnings regarding how this data should be used or interpreted.

Keep Formatting Simple

Please avoid using complex Excel formatting like merged cells, custom cell colors, or multiple lines inside a single cell. Plain text ensures the smoothest conversion to the web platform!

docs.title: Submitting Your Changes
docs.text:
Once your Excel file is ready and reviewed:

  • Upload the new version to the designated shared drive.
  • Notify the database administration team via email or our internal chat.
  • The team will process the file, and your changes will be live on the Data Dictionary within a few minutes!

docs.title: Schema overview
docs.text:
The public schema is organised around three groups of tables:

  1. Enterprises: the owned, located units that can be damaged (buildings, farms, businesses, network systems).
  2. Components: the physical or economic elements that belong to an enterprise (crops, machinery, staff, road segments, and so on).
  3. Assessment: events, surveys and the damage records they produce.

Enterprises and components both use table-per-subtype inheritance: a sub-type table shares the primary key of its parent, so a row is joined to its parent with child.id = parent.id.

The schema is shown in three diagrams to keep each one readable.

docs.text:
Different name in the web-app (GUI)

In the PostgreSQL backend, this table is named building, as shown in the page title. In the web-app interface it appears as Built environment. All aliases are listed in the correspondence table.

Description (EN): This table represents buildings. In the database's inheritance architecture, it acts as a direct sub-type of the enterprise table. It does not store redundant descriptive columns; instead, it uses a shared primary key to inherit all high-level attributes (such as name, location, management type, and geometry) from its parent enterprise record.

The structural, economic and physical characteristics of a building (construction year, materials, number of floors, cost, and so on) are stored in the building_component table.

docs.title: Column Structure
docs.text: Column Data type Definition Example value Constraint? Geometry? Comments id BIGINT Building unique identifier 3 PK, FK No Primary key that also acts as a Foreign Key referencing enterprise.id

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Inherits from (Sub-type of): enterprise. The building table is a specialized extension of the enterprise table.
  • Contains: While not linked directly via a building_id, a building owns its physical parts through the enterprise_id column in the component table. These components often include specialized sub-types such as:
    • building_component
    • added_block
    • building_functionality

Where is the rest of the data?

To find the name, geographical location (geometry, town, country), or VAT of a building, you must join this table with the enterprise record that shares the exact same id. The structural and economic characteristics are in building_component, which is linked to the building through component.enterprise_id.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve the characteristics of each building by joining its enterprise record with its building components:

SELECT
    e.name,
    e.town,
    bc.n_floors,
    bc.construction_cost,
    bc.economic_value
FROM
    building b
JOIN
    enterprise e ON b.id = e.id
JOIN
    component c ON c.enterprise_id = e.id
JOIN
    building_component bc ON bc.id = c.id
WHERE
    e.type = 'BUILDING';

docs.title: Table: enterprise
docs.text: Description (EN): This is the core parent entity (superclass) of the database. It stores the universal, high-level attributes, such as identification, geographical location and administrative details, for all major physical or business assets. Specific types of enterprises (like buildings, businesses, farms or network systems) store their specialized data in separate sub-tables that share the same ID. Ownership is not stored here: it is recorded in the bridge table enterprise_owner.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
Because enterprise is the central hub of the schema, it has extensive relationships:

  • Has Sub-types (Inheritance): The following tables inherit from enterprise and share its id:
    • building
    • business
    • farm
    • network_system
  • Is owned by: owner. An enterprise can have several owners, and an owner can hold several enterprises. This many-to-many relationship is mediated by the enterprise_owner bridge table.
  • Has many: component (An enterprise is composed of multiple sub-components like machinery, crops, or electrical networks)
  • Has many: survey (An enterprise can undergo multiple damage or assessment surveys over time)

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve a list of all enterprises located in a specific town, displaying their name, their specific classification (type), and their coordinates:

SELECT 
    id, 
    name, 
    type, 
    ST_AsText(geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    enterprise 
WHERE 
    town = 'Rome'
ORDER BY 
    type ASC;

Retrieve the owners of each enterprise through the bridge table:

SELECT 
    e.id, 
    e.name, 
    o.full_name 
FROM 
    enterprise e
JOIN 
    enterprise_owner eo ON eo.enterprise_id = e.id
JOIN 
    owner o ON o.id = eo.owner_id;

docs.title: Table: farm
docs.text:
Different name in the web-app (GUI)

In the PostgreSQL backend, this table is named farm, as shown in the page title. In the web-app interface it appears as Economic Activities - Farm. All aliases are listed in the correspondence table.

Description (EN): This table represents agricultural enterprises. In the database's inheritance architecture, it acts as a direct sub-type of the enterprise table. It does not store redundant descriptive columns; instead, it uses a shared primary key to inherit all high-level attributes (such as name, location, management type, and geometry) from its parent enterprise record.

docs.title: Column Structure
docs.text: Column Data type Definition Example value Constraint? Geometry? Comments id BIGINT Unique identifier for the farm 42 PK, FK No Primary key that also acts as a Foreign Key referencing enterprise.id

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Inherits from (Sub-type of): enterprise. The farm table is a specialized extension of the enterprise table.
  • Contains: While not linked directly via a farm_id, a farm owns agricultural assets through the enterprise_id column in the component table. These components often include specialized agricultural sub-types such as:
    • agriculture_product and its sub-types crop and stored
    • livestock
    • fixed_asset and its sub-types (e.g. machinery such as tractors)

Where is the rest of the data?

To find the name, geographical location (geometry, town, country), or other details of a farm, you must join this table with the enterprise record that shares the exact same id.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve a list of all farms, including their names, towns, and spatial coordinates, by joining the table with its parent enterprise entity:

SELECT 
    f.id, 
    e.name, 
    e.town, 
    ST_AsText(e.geometry) as coordinates 
FROM 
    farm f
JOIN 
    enterprise e ON f.id = e.id
WHERE 
    e.type = 'FARM';

docs.text: Description (EN): This table represents damages reported to farms. In the database's inheritance architecture, it acts as a direct sub-type of the damage table. It does not store redundant descriptive columns; instead, it uses a shared primary key to inherit all high-level attributes (such as description, dates, location and geometry) from its parent damage record.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Inherits from (Sub-type of): damage. The farm_damage table is a specialized extension of the damage table.
  • Affects: component (One or more damages affect a component or its subclasses)
  • Is reported by: survey (One or more damages is reported in a survey)
  • Reported in: attachment (A damage is reported in one or more attachments)
  • Results in: economic_loss
  • Has Sub-types (Inheritance): The following tables inherit from farm_damage and share its id:
    • damage_agriculture_product
    • damage_fixed_asset
    • damage_livestock
    • damage_provision
    • damage_staff

Where is the rest of the data?

To find the description, dates, geographical location (geometry, town, country), or other details of a damage to farms, you must join this table with the damage record that shares the exact same id.

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
Retrieve a list of all damages to farms, including their descriptions, towns, and spatial coordinates, by joining the table with its parent damage entity:

SELECT
    fd.*,
    d.*
FROM 
    farm_damage fd JOIN damage d ON fd.id = d.id;
